headline: A raw Kentucky Friday brings showers and a few possible nonaccumulating flakes; both regions then turn dry with repeated nighttime freezes
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A deep upper trough and reinforcing impulse keep Central Kentucky cloudy, raw and intermittently showery today. Freezing levels near 2,000–3,000 feet and steep low-level lapse rates allow a heavier shower to briefly mix with wet snow or graupel, but warm ground and above-freezing surface temperatures prevent accumulation around Danville and Lexington. The disturbance exits tonight, then high pressure brings a dry weekend, increasing sunshine and repeated nighttime freezes.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 6:55 AM EST, KDVK reported 36°F with a 34°F dew point, northwest wind near 7 mph, visibility above 10 miles and an overcast ceiling near 1,200 feet. At 6:54 AM, KLEX reported 38°F with a 35°F dew point, northwest wind near 8 mph, light rain, 10-mile visibility and an overcast 700-foot ceiling. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final issuance check.

days.label: Friday / Friday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. Independent concerns are brief rain or mixed rain/snow showers, raw wind chills and a widespread freeze tonight. A few wet flakes or graupel may reach Danville, but no accumulation or travel impact is expected.
days.forecast: Cloudy, raw conditions continue with intermittent cellular showers from morning through late afternoon, tapering mainly between 6 PM and 10 PM. The most-likely Danville high is near 43°F. Northwest wind runs 8–14 mph with gusts of 18–25 mph. A stronger shower may briefly mix with wet snow or graupel, but any flakes should melt on contact. Clouds gradually break tonight, supporting a most-likely Saturday-morning low near 28°F, with middle-20s readings in colder rural valleys. Thunder, heavy rain and dense fog are not expected.

days.label: Saturday / Saturday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Saturday at issuance. Independent concern is a widespread freeze early Saturday and again Saturday night. Any early stray flurry should remain east of Danville; rain, accumulating snow, thunder and advisory-level wind are not forecast.
days.forecast: Any early stray flurry remains mainly east of Danville. Morning stratocumulus gives way to mostly sunny, dry weather as high pressure builds in. The most-likely Danville high is near 46°F. Northwest wind of 3–8 mph may occasionally gust 10–16 mph before easing. Clear sky and light wind Saturday night promote another most-likely low near 28°F, with colder valleys in the middle 20s.

days.label: Sunday / early Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Sunday at issuance. Independent concern is another widespread freeze Sunday night into Monday morning. Patchy frost is likely, while any valley fog should remain isolated and brief.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and dry conditions continue while midlevel heights rise modestly. The most-likely Danville high is near 50°F. North to northeast wind runs 1–6 mph and becomes nearly calm at night. Clear sky, low humidity and light wind favor a most-likely early-Monday low near 28°F, with colder rural valleys in the middle 20s. An isolated valley fog pocket is possible near dawn, but widespread dense fog is not supported.

kentucky.bottomLine: Danville stays raw and showery today, and a heavier shower may contain wet snow or graupel without accumulation. Most-likely temperatures are 43/28°F Friday and Friday night, 46/28°F Saturday and Saturday night, and 50/28°F Sunday and Sunday night. The weekend is dry with increasing sunshine and repeated freezes.
kentucky.confidence: Moderate-high on Friday temperatures, showers and wind; moderate on whether Danville observes flakes; high on a dry weekend; moderate-high on daytime highs and moderate on exact radiational-cooling lows

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: The Clemson–Central corridor remains in a dry northwest-flow sector beneath the deep eastern trough. Sunshine and downslope mixing lift temperatures into the middle 50s today despite continued cold advection. Canadian high pressure settles closer Saturday and produces the coldest night of the period under clear, calm conditions. Heights rise slightly Sunday, but the dry continental air mass persists. No rain, snow or thunder is expected in the corridor.
upstate.currentConditions: At 6:54 AM EST, KCEU reported 38°F with a 33°F dew point, west wind near 10 mph, clear sky and unrestricted visibility. At 7:15 AM, KLQK reported 34°F with a 32°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and unrestricted visibility. KAND and KGSP were also clear at 6:56 and 6:53 AM. No official NWS point alert was active for Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Friday / Friday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concern is a freeze tonight, especially around KLQK and sheltered Pickens County hollows. GSP has ended seasonal freeze products, so the absence of a Freeze Warning does not remove the risk.
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and cool weather continues beneath the eastern trough. Most-likely highs are near 57°F at KCEU and 56°F at KLQK. West-northwest wind runs 5–10 mph with gusts of 18–24 mph before easing tonight. Most-likely Saturday-morning lows are near 36°F at KCEU and 30°F at KLQK. The regional freeze probability is about 75%, highest around Central and colder hollows; the chance of 28°F or colder is roughly 25% in the coldest terrain.

days.label: Saturday / Saturday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active. Independent concern is a widespread freeze Saturday night into Sunday morning, with hard-freeze readings possible in colder hollows. Seasonal freeze products have ended; rain, snow, thunder and advisory-level wind are not forecast in the corridor.
days.forecast: Sunny and dry weather continues as Canadian high pressure settles closer. Most-likely highs are near 56°F at KCEU and 55°F at KLQK. North-northwest wind of 3–7 mph may occasionally gust 10–15 mph before becoming light or calm. Clear sky and strong decoupling make Saturday night the coldest of the period. Most-likely early-Sunday lows are near 33°F at KCEU and 27°F at KLQK, with colder hollows in the middle 20s. The regional freeze probability is about 95%.

days.label: Sunday / early Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active. Independent concern is another freeze Sunday night into Monday morning, focused on KLQK, rural Pickens County and sheltered hollows. Rain, snow, thunder and advisory-level wind are not forecast.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and dry conditions continue as heights rise modestly and weak return flow begins. Most-likely highs are near 57°F at KCEU and 56°F at KLQK. Light and variable wind becomes west-southwest around 1–5 mph by afternoon and light northeast overnight. Most-likely early-Monday lows are near 36°F at KCEU and 31°F at KLQK. The regional freeze probability is about 65%, concentrated around Central and sheltered terrain.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor stays sunny and dry through Sunday. Most-likely station values are KCEU 57/36°F, 56/33°F and 57/36°F and KLQK 56/30°F, 55/27°F and 56/31°F. Independent regional freeze probabilities are about 75% tonight, 95% Saturday night and 65% Sunday night.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather and sky conditions; moderate-high on daytime highs and wind; moderate on exact nighttime lows because station and terrain differences increase after decoupling

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERTS: no active NWS point alert was present for Danville, Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. Official alerts remain explicitly separate from national outlooks and this independent analysis.

The 11:34Z Louisville discussion supports scattered Kentucky showers today, rain as the principal type, a brief rain/snow or graupel mix in stronger showers, freezing levels near 2,000–3,000 feet, northwest wind and rapid melting of any flakes. High pressure then brings a dry weekend and repeated freezes.

Chris Bailey’s exact November 13 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘A Few Festive Flakes Flying,’ and its readable graphics were consulted as accepted authoritative source material. Bailey supports upper-30s/lower-40s temperatures, gusty wind and rounds of rain and a few snow showers today and tonight; his map places Danville in the ‘a few flakes possible’ zone while reserving light accumulation for far southeastern high terrain. Details absent or unreadable were left unknown.

The 11:25Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussion supports dry, gusty northwest flow in the Clemson–Central corridor, widespread freezes Friday and Saturday nights, the coldest readings Saturday night and no corridor snow. Seasonal freeze products have ended, so the lack of a warning is not evidence against the independent freeze probabilities.

Official point guidance supports Danville near 44/28°F, 46/28°F and 49/28°F; Clemson near 57/34°F, 56/30°F and 57/33°F; and Central near 56/33°F, 56/29°F and 56/33°F. The independent cards preserve these centers within the empirically calibrated widths and apply the maintained station corrections in the prose.
Current observations showed low cloud and light rain at KLEX and raw northwest flow at KDVK, while KCEU, KLQK, KAND and KGSP were clear and dry. Tempest was excluded.

COD radar at 12:10Z showed scattered light wraparound returns mainly north and east of Danville and no meaningful Upstate echoes. Infrared imagery at 12:11:17Z showed cyclonic stratocumulus over Kentucky/Tennessee, a clearer inland Upstate and organized deep cloud offshore.

The current 00Z COD 500-mb vorticity and 700-mb humidity analyses support the deep Great Lakes–Ohio Valley trough, northwest flow and progressive drying. COD surface temperature/SLP, 850-mb dewpoint and precipitable-water panels resolved to older dates and were explicitly excluded as stale.

Every currently visible COD family was audited: HRRR, RAP, RRFS, GEM-RDPS, GEM-GDPS, ECMWF, GFS, AIFS, AIGFS, CFSv2, GEFS, REFS, AIFS-ENS and AIGEFS. NAM, NAM Nest, SREF, HREF and HiresW are retired and were not used as current guidance.

The COD deterministic and ensemble consensus supports roughly 0.03–0.20 inch of Kentucky wraparound precipitation, concentrated Friday, followed by dry weather. All Upstate families are dry except an AIGFS trace. Ensemble 850-mb means agree on the coldest air Saturday followed by gradual moderation.

Kentucky radiational lows are the main model disagreement: RDPS/GDPS are substantially colder than ECMWF/GFS/AI guidance Sunday and Monday mornings. REFS, NBM, GEFS, official guidance and KLEX BUFKIT favor the warmer camp, while clear rural Danville can undercut KLEX. The calibrated eight-degree low ranges retain this tail without treating it as an unresolved blocker.

Fresh BUFKIT profiles used HRRR/RAP 10Z and RRFS 06Z plus GFS 00Z for KLEX, KAND and KGSP. KLEX supports a 43–45°F Friday high and light QPF; KAND/KGSP support 53–57°F and zero QPF. Partial horizons were not extrapolated.

The installed BUFKIT 19 working-data set at C:\Users\Public\Bufkit\Data refreshed KLEX/KSME guidance through 11:47Z. Older bundled sample/archive files in the separate program installation were excluded; today’s downloaded KAND/KGSP profiles supplied the fresh Upstate proxy guidance.
The local GRIB package was generated at 2026-11-13T12:43:59Z. HRRR, RAP, GFS, GEFS and ECMWF were used only within their validated horizons; partial periods were not extrapolated.
Central Kentucky’s most-likely values are 43/28°F, 46/28°F and 50/28°F. The maintained KDVK −1.5°F low correction, official guidance, GEFS/NBM and terrain context support the nighttime centers.

A few Kentucky flakes remain a conditional occurrence forecast, not an accumulation forecast. Bailey and Louisville support flakes; warm ground, above-freezing surface temperatures and light precipitation support no sticking or travel impact around Danville.

Upstate most-likely values are KCEU 57/36°F, 56/33°F and 57/36°F and KLQK 56/30°F, 55/27°F and 56/31°F. The maintained KCEU +2°F and KLQK −3°F low corrections are applied; the cards retain the required 10°F regional low widths for station and terrain spread.

SPC Days 1–3 provide no relevant severe-weather area for either corridor, and WPC Days 1–3 provide no relevant excessive-rain threat. National outlooks are not point alerts. Thunder, heavy rain and flooding are unsupported.
The latest completed accuracy summary contains 139 verified checkpoints and all-category accuracy of 80.3% overall, including 84.1% for Central Kentucky and 76.4% for the Upstate.
Current station corrections, empirical lead-specific temperature widths, regime-aware verified weights, conditional fog handling, explicit event timing and official-alert separation were applied.

Temperature cards use the current calibrated regional widths: Kentucky high/low widths of 5/8°F, 6/8°F and 7/8°F; Upstate widths of 4/10°F, 5/10°F and 6/10°F. Prose provides narrower station-specific most-likely values.
All local times use Eastern Standard Time. The third card includes Sunday night and early Monday because validThrough is exactly 72 elapsed hours after issuance.
